What do these measures mean?
Treasury
Coin available for works and decisions; the weekly change is itemized above.
Granaries
Food stores. The realm eats weekly and gathers one harvest each autumn; grain is not bought directly.
Levies
Soldiers available to defend the realm and answer a muster.
Legitimacy
Belief in the Crown’s right to rule. If it falls too far, the chair is lost.
Piety
The Crown’s standing with the Flame and the religious life of the realm.
Prosperity
The health of the towns. It raises taxes and harvests, but also the cost of court.

How to Play

You are the Crown. Time flows on its own (pause with ❚❚). Letters arrive; your choices bend the realm. Set taxes, tolls, tithe and levy pay with the sliders. Spend the treasury on works — mills and dams raise the harvest and the tax base, villages grow into towns, walls and beacons ready you for a war you can fund but never command. As settlements swell from village to town to city, greater works unlock — markets, stone roads and a guildhall enrich the purse, and a city may raise a university, a cathedral, or a sea-harbor; locked works show the tier they still require. Once a harbor opens the sea, you may mount expeditions past the last chart — each returns a captain's letter: a discovery, a peril, or word of a realm across the Sundered Sea. Works take seasons to build. Barges pay toll passing the capital; the river freezes in winter and the tolls with it. Raise men-at-arms, ride royal progresses, and pay informants to sharpen the whispers. Your reign autosaves in this browser; “Copy history link” makes a link that replays your exact reign anywhere. Survive twenty years and the crown passes to your heir — or lose it, and take it back.

For agents at the helm (or humans in the console):

annals.state()        // full public game state as JSON
annals.choices()      // pending letter, if any
annals.choose(i)      // answer the letter with option i
annals.setSlider(k,v) // 'tax'|'toll'|'tithe'|'pay'
annals.build(key)     // e.g. annals.build('mill')
annals.builds()       // available works + costs
annals.speed(0..3)    // 0 pauses
annals.advance(n)     // step n weeks while paused
annals.chronicle(n)   // last n chronicle entries
annals.spy()          // pay informants (80 gold)
annals.history()      // shareable link that replays this reign

Same seed + same actions on the same weeks = the same history. Share a realm with #s=<seed>.

The Codex of the Realm

A reader's index to the reign and the House that holds it — persons, places, houses, wyrms, and the crowns already closed, with the years they surface. Read-only; the record as it stands. Given names may recur in the realm; title, office, and House identify the person meant.

The Colophon

The making of the book, and the levers that tend it. v—

The Realm, and How It Sounds

Procedural ambience — the river, the wind, the year-bell, a scratch of the pen as each letter arrives. Off until you ask; makes no sound the reign depends on.

The Saved Reigns

A named snapshot, kept in this browser — the reign as it stands, every choice remembered. Restore one to sit that chair again; each is also a shareable link. (The reign already autosaves per seed; these are the ones you name and keep.)

Keep It on the Table

On a phone or tablet, add The Cold Chair to your home screen from the browser menu — it opens full-screen, like a book you keep by the chair. One file, one link: the whole game travels in the page you are reading.

How the Book Is Bound

One HTML file. No servers, no accounts, no store — the reign lives in the page. A reign is a pure function of its seed and the choices you made, so a history link carries the whole telling: hand someone the link and they watch the same reign, letter for letter, down to the last leaf.

The letters, the map, the marginal notes, the monk’s judgment, and the ambience are all made at the moment you read them — nothing is fetched, nothing is stored elsewhere. What you play is what you can post.

After Whom

Built in the spirit of emollick/annals-kingdom, and in debt to King of Dragon Pass for the lesson that a letter should remember. The factions here scheme on their own procedural agendas; the armies are never yours to command.

The Last Leaf

One page: the map as it ended, the reign’s five defining moments, the monk’s judgment, and the link that replays it all.
